mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in FEDFUNDS exceeds +0.25%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to reduced real interest rates encouraging equity investment.
regime_hint: FED Funds rate normalization or easing phase
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average of the prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 2% above the prior month's level is associated with a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return, reflecting stronger labor market momentum.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly above the 20-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) rises by more than 5% in the prior month versus the month before, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to over-heating demand and potential profit compression.
failure_condition: Over 6 months, the average 20-day forward return during such events is not statistically lower than during stable demand periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 3% for two consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak supply growth raises inflation expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < INDPRO previous month and INDPRO < INDPRO two months ago
failure_condition: During such supply shocks, the 20-day forward return is not significantly below the 30-day rolling mean (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for three consecutive months, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as lower labor costs support equity valuations.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during such episodes are not higher than the 20-day average of the prior 12 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE by at least 0.5 percentage points indicates mixed labor market signals, which predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return due to policy uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 0.5% AND UNRATE > previous month + 0.5%
failure_condition: During such interaction events, the 20-day forward return is not significantly lower than the mean of non-interaction events (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in CPIAUCSL (CPI) of at least 0.3% for four consecutive months suggests disinflation, which is associated with a positive S&P 60-day forward return as rate-cut expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < previous month and CPIAUCSL < month-1 and CPIAUCSL < month-2 and CPIAUCSL < month-3 by at least 0.3%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns during such episodes are not higher than the 20-day average of the prior 18 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of GDPC1 (GDP) growth turns negative, the S&P 20-day forward return is predicted to be negative due to economic softening and reduced equity risk appetite.
regime_hint: Economic softening detected via GDP growth
failure_condition: During negative GDP growth periods, the 20-day forward return is not statistically lower than the 20-day average of positive GDP growth periods (t-test p > 0.05).
